title: Trigonometric identities

points.text: Double-angle identities for sin and cos
Finding one ratio from another (using sign and quadrant)

bigPicture: Identities link sin, cos and tan so you can find one from another or simplify expressions. The double-angle identities return in calculus and trig equations.

keyIdeas.answer: sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 2cos²θ − 1 = 1 − 2sin²θ.

keyIdeas.cue: Find tan θ from sin θ = 3/5, θ obtuse?

keyTerms.def: true for every value of the variable (≡)

workedExamples.title: Double angle
workedExamples.prompt: sin θ = 1/3, θ acute. Find sin 2θ exactly.

misconceptions.right: It is 2 sin θ cos θ.

misconceptions.wrong: Ignoring quadrant when taking square roots

practice.prompt: Show that (sin θ + cos θ)² ≡ 1 + sin 2θ.
solution: LHS = sin²θ + 2 sin θ cos θ + cos²θ
commonErrors: Working on both sides at once

practice.prompt: cos θ = −0.4 with π < θ < 3π/2. Find sin θ and cos 2θ.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

given.item: Pythagorean identity; double-angle identities for sin and cos

formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.
